all_evidence.title: Association of iron supplementation with risk of transfusion, hospital length of stay, and mortality in geriatric patients undergoing hip fracture surgeries: a meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Chen R; Li L; Xiang Z; Li H; Hou XL
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.outcome: The outcomes were blood transfusion rate and volume, length of stay, infection and mortality (last follow-up). | RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02). | A significant reduction was detected in transfusion volume (two studies: n = 234; MD - 0.45 units/patient, 95% CI - 0.74 to - 0.16; P = 0.002), hospital stay (five studies: n = 998; MD - 1.42, 95% CI - 2.18 to - 0.67; P = 0.0002) and caused no increased risk of mortality (five studies: n = 937; OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.65-1.36; P = 0.76) and infection (four studies: n = 701; OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.90; P = 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 메타분석(6개 연구: 환자 1201명)에서 철분 보충제는 수혈률 감소와 관련이 없었으나(OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69) 높은 이질성(I2 = 61%)이 확인됐고, 연구 4편에 대한 민감도 분석에서는 유의한 관련성이 확인됐다(n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.population: AIMS: To assess the efficacy and safety of iron supplementation for perioperative anemia in geriatric patients with hip fracture. | METHODS: A systematic search was conducted for studies published using PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library Databases that compared iron supplementation with placebo in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. | Sub-group analyses of four studies showed that the preoperative intravenous use of iron at 200-300 mg (two studies) may be the beneficial option for hip fractures patients.

all_evidence.title: Effectiveness of Iron Supplementation With or Without Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents on Red Blood Cell Utilization in Patients With Preoperative Anaemia Undergoing Elective Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Van Remoortel H; Laermans J; Avau B; Bekkering G; Georgsen J; Manzini PM; Meybohm P; Ozier Y; De Buck E; Compernolle V; Vandekerckhove P
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 우리는 다음을 확인했다: (1) 정맥 및/또는 경구 철분 단독요법은 수혈된 단위 수를 줄이지 못할 수 있고 정맥 철분은 수혈받은 환자 수를 감소시키지 못할 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (2) 철분요법의 투여 경로(정맥 대 경구)가 적혈구 사용량에 다르게 영향을 주는지는 불확실하다(매우 낮은 확실성 근거); (3) 정맥 페릭 카르복시말토스 단독요법은 정맥 철분 수크로스 단독요법과 비교해 수혈받은 환자 수에 차이를 만들지 못할 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (4) 경구 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자 수와 수혈 단위 수를 감소시킬 가능성이 있다(중등도 확실성 근거); (5) 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자 수를 감소시킬 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (6) 경구 및/또는 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자에서 수혈된 적혈구 단위 수를 감소시킬 가능성이 있다(중등도 확실성 근거); (7) 경구 및/또는 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제가 여러 단위의 수혈을 필요로 하는 환자 수에 미치는 영향은 불확실하다(매우 낮은 확실성 근거).
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Xiao F; Han W; Yue Q; Ke J; Jia B; Fu X

evidence.venue: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_1: AIM: Preoperative anaemia is associated with increased morbidity and mortality.
evidence.outcome: AIM: Preoperative anaemia is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. | Our main outcomes were absolute increase in haemoglobin, blood transfusion rate and postoperative morbidity. | All studies showed a decreased blood transfusion rate following iron supplementation.

evidence.title: Fish Oil and Perioperative Bleeding.

evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_3: Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo.

evidence.key_finding: Methods and Results We tested the effect of fish oil supplementation on perioperative bleeding in a multinational, placebo-controlled trial involving 1516 patients who were randomized to perioperative fish oil (eicosapentaenoic acid+docosahexaenoic acid; 8-10 g for 2-5 days preoperatively, and then 2 g/d postoperatively) or placebo.

evidence.title: Association of iron supplementation with risk of transfusion, hospital length of stay, and mortality in geriatric patients undergoing hip fracture surgeries: a meta-analysis.
evidence.authors: Chen R; Li L; Xiang Z; Li H; Hou XL
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
evidence.outcome: The outcomes were blood transfusion rate and volume, length of stay, infection and mortality (last follow-up). | RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02). | A significant reduction was detected in transfusion volume (two studies: n = 234; MD - 0.45 units/patient, 95% CI - 0.74 to - 0.16; P = 0.002), hospital stay (five studies: n = 998; MD - 1.42, 95% CI - 2.18 to - 0.67; P = 0.0002) and caused no increased risk of mortality (five studies: n = 937; OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.65-1.36; P = 0.76) and infection (four studies: n = 701; OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.90; P = 0.01).
evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 메타분석(6개 연구: 환자 1201명)에서 철분 보충제는 수혈률 감소와 관련이 없었으나(OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69) 높은 이질성(I2 = 61%)이 확인됐고, 연구 4편에 대한 민감도 분석에서는 유의한 관련성이 확인됐다(n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
evidence.population: AIMS: To assess the efficacy and safety of iron supplementation for perioperative anemia in geriatric patients with hip fracture. | METHODS: A systematic search was conducted for studies published using PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library Databases that compared iron supplementation with placebo in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. | Sub-group analyses of four studies showed that the preoperative intravenous use of iron at 200-300 mg (two studies) may be the beneficial option for hip fractures patients.

all_evidence.title: Effectiveness of Iron Supplementation With or Without Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents on Red Blood Cell Utilization in Patients With Preoperative Anaemia Undergoing Elective Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Van Remoortel H; Laermans J; Avau B; Bekkering G; Georgsen J; Manzini PM; Meybohm P; Ozier Y; De Buck E; Compernolle V; Vandekerckhove P
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 우리는 다음을 확인했다: (1) 정맥 및/또는 경구 철분 단독요법은 수혈된 단위 수를 줄이지 못할 수 있고 정맥 철분은 수혈받은 환자 수를 감소시키지 못할 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (2) 철분요법의 투여 경로(정맥 대 경구)가 적혈구 사용량에 다르게 영향을 주는지는 불확실하다(매우 낮은 확실성 근거); (3) 정맥 페릭 카르복시말토스 단독요법은 정맥 철분 수크로스 단독요법과 비교해 수혈받은 환자 수에 차이를 만들지 못할 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (4) 경구 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자 수와 수혈 단위 수를 감소시킬 가능성이 있다(중등도 확실성 근거); (5) 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자 수를 감소시킬 수 있다(낮은 확실성 근거); (6) 경구 및/또는 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제는 수혈받은 환자에서 수혈된 적혈구 단위 수를 감소시킬 가능성이 있다(중등도 확실성 근거); (7) 경구 및/또는 정맥 철분 + 조혈자극제가 여러 단위의 수혈을 필요로 하는 환자 수에 미치는 영향은 불확실하다(매우 낮은 확실성 근거).

all_evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Association of iron supplementation with risk of transfusion, hospital length of stay, and mortality in geriatric patients undergoing hip fracture surgeries: a meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Chen R; Li L; Xiang Z; Li H; Hou XL
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.outcome: The outcomes were blood transfusion rate and volume, length of stay, infection and mortality (last follow-up). | RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02). | A significant reduction was detected in transfusion volume (two studies: n = 234; MD - 0.45 units/patient, 95% CI - 0.74 to - 0.16; P = 0.002), hospital stay (five studies: n = 998; MD - 1.42, 95% CI - 2.18 to - 0.67; P = 0.0002) and caused no increased risk of mortality (five studies: n = 937; OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.65-1.36; P = 0.76) and infection (four studies: n = 701; OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.90; P = 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 메타분석(6개 연구: 환자 1201명)에서 철분 보충제는 수혈률 감소와 관련이 없었으나(OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69) 높은 이질성(I2 = 61%)이 확인됐고, 연구 4편에 대한 민감도 분석에서는 유의한 관련성이 확인됐다(n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.population: AIMS: To assess the efficacy and safety of iron supplementation for perioperative anemia in geriatric patients with hip fracture. | METHODS: A systematic search was conducted for studies published using PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library Databases that compared iron supplementation with placebo in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. | Sub-group analyses of four studies showed that the preoperative intravenous use of iron at 200-300 mg (two studies) may be the beneficial option for hip fractures patients.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative intravenous versus oral iron supplementation for elective surgery: evidence based on 12 randomized trials.
all_evidence.authors: Yue L; Zhang J; Li C; Wang Z; Qi L; Zhao Y; Wang S; Shang M; Li C; Sun H
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: IVIS was associated with fewer digestive (RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) but more pain-related adverse events (RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.outcome: AIM: This study aims to clarify hematological parameters, transfusion requirements, and adverse events of preoperative intravenous (IVIS) versus oral iron supplementation (OIS) in elective surgery patients. | Our analysis focused on post-treatment hemoglobin levels, changes in hemoglobin from baseline, ferritin levels, hemoglobin attainment rates, transfusion requirements, and adverse events. | No significant differences were noted in transfusion rates or volumes.
all_evidence.key_finding: IVIS was associated with fewer digestive (RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) but more pain-related adverse events (RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 정맥 철분 보충은 소화기계 이상반응은 더 적었으나(RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) 통증 관련 이상반응은 더 많았다(RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.population: AIM: This study aims to clarify hematological parameters, transfusion requirements, and adverse events of preoperative intravenous (IVIS) versus oral iron supplementation (OIS) in elective surgery patients. | INTERPRETATION: IVIS offers a superior improvement in hematological parameters for elective surgery patients but not reducing transfusion needs compared to OIS.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative iron supplementation in non-anemic patients undergoing major surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Toledo FV; De Carli D; Meletti JFA; Togo HYA; Gomes IP; Sakashita RM; Montes LF; Tiburcio RS; Miranda CA
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Preoperative iron supplementation was associated with a significantly lower risk of receiving a blood transfusion (OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Blood transfusions are associated with increased morbidity and mortality, and maintaining global blood supplies can be a challenge. | This systematic review investigates the impact of preoperative iron supplementation on the risk of blood transfusion among non-anemic patients undergoing major surgeries. | Outcomes assessed included the number of individuals who received blood transfusions, and mean hemoglobin levels at the first day and by the first postoperative week.
all_evidence.key_finding: Preoperative iron supplementation was associated with a significantly lower risk of receiving a blood transfusion (OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 수술 전 철분 보충은 수혈을 받을 위험이 유의하게 더 낮은 것과 관련이 있었다(OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.population: This systematic review investigates the impact of preoperative iron supplementation on the risk of blood transfusion among non-anemic patients undergoing major surgeries. | Outcomes assessed included the number of individuals who received blood transfusions, and mean hemoglobin levels at the first day and by the first postoperative week. | Of these, 54% received preoperative iron supplementation.

all_evidence.title: Association of iron supplementation with risk of transfusion, hospital length of stay, and mortality in geriatric patients undergoing hip fracture surgeries: a meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Chen R; Li L; Xiang Z; Li H; Hou XL
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.outcome: The outcomes were blood transfusion rate and volume, length of stay, infection and mortality (last follow-up). | RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02). | A significant reduction was detected in transfusion volume (two studies: n = 234; MD - 0.45 units/patient, 95% CI - 0.74 to - 0.16; P = 0.002), hospital stay (five studies: n = 998; MD - 1.42, 95% CI - 2.18 to - 0.67; P = 0.0002) and caused no increased risk of mortality (five studies: n = 937; OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.65-1.36; P = 0.76) and infection (four studies: n = 701; OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.90; P = 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding: RESULTS: The meta-analysis (6 studies: 1201 patients) indicated that iron supplements were not associated with reducing blood transfusion rate (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69), but high heterogeneity (I2 = 61%) was detected and a significant association was found in sensitivity analysis of four studies (n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결과: 메타분석(6개 연구: 환자 1201명)에서 철분 보충제는 수혈률 감소와 관련이 없었으나(OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.60-1.41; P = 0.69) 높은 이질성(I2 = 61%)이 확인됐고, 연구 4편에 대한 민감도 분석에서는 유의한 관련성이 확인됐다(n = 637; OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02).
all_evidence.population: AIMS: To assess the efficacy and safety of iron supplementation for perioperative anemia in geriatric patients with hip fracture. | METHODS: A systematic search was conducted for studies published using PubMed, EMBASE and Cochrane Library Databases that compared iron supplementation with placebo in patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. | Sub-group analyses of four studies showed that the preoperative intravenous use of iron at 200-300 mg (two studies) may be the beneficial option for hip fractures patients.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_8: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.outcome: Patient Blood Management (PBM) is an evidence-based, multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to optimizing the care of patients who might need a blood transfusion. | Primary outcomes were the number of patients and the number of RBC units transfused. | We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).
all_evidence.key_finding: We found that: (1) IV and/or oral iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of units transfused and IV iron may not reduce the number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (2) uncertainty exists whether the administration route of iron therapy (IV vs oral) differentially affects RBC utilization (very low-certainty evidence); (3) IV ferric carboxymaltose monotherapy may not result in a different number of patients transfused compared to IV iron sucrose monotherapy (low-certainty evidence); (4) oral iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of patients transfused and number of units transfused (moderate-certainty evidence); (5) IV iron + ESAs may result in a reduced number of patients transfused (low-certainty evidence); (6) oral and/or IV iron + ESAs probably results in a reduced number of RBC units transfused in transfused patients (moderate-certainty evidence); (7) uncertainty exists about the effect of oral and/or IV iron + ESAs on the number of patients requiring transfusion of multiple units (very low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: This systematic review aimed to collect the best available evidence on the effectiveness of preoperative iron supplementation with or without erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) on red blood cell (RBC) utilization in all-cause anaemic patients scheduled for elective surgery. | We identified 29 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and 2 non-RCTs comparing the effectiveness of preoperative iron monotherapy, or iron + ESAs, to control (no treatment, usual care, placebo). | In conclusion, in patients with anaemia of any cause scheduled for elective surgery, the preoperative administration of iron monotherapy may not result in a reduced number of patients or units transfused (low-certainty evidence).

all_evidence.title: Perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Xiao F; Han W; Yue Q; Ke J; Jia B; Fu X
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_6: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.outcome: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.key_finding: Overall, compared with control group for liver surgery, omega-3 fatty acids were associated with substantially reduced incidence of infection (odd ratio [OR]=0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI] =0.34-0.91; P = .02), but revealed no remarkable influence on complications (OR = 0.60; 95% CI = 0.29-1.24; P = .17), mortality (OR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.06-9.37; P = .83), liver failure (OR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.10 to 5.00; P = 0.74), biliary leakage (OR=1.24; 95% CI = 0.41 to 3.76; P = .70), bleeding (OR = 1.76; 95% CI = 0.63-4.95; P = .28), or ileus (OR = 0.39; 95% CI = 0.07-2.05; P = .27).
all_evidence.population: INTRODUCTION: The effect of perioperative omega-3 fatty acids for liver surgery remained controversial. | We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to explore the influence of omega-3 fatty acids versus placebo in patients undergoing liver surgery. | METHODS: We have searched PubMed, EMbase, Web of science, EBSCO, and Cochrane library databases through May 2020, and included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing the effect of omega-3 fatty acids versus placebo for liver surgery.

all_evidence.title: Effects of intraoperative or postoperative administration of intravenous iron supplements on hemoglobin recovery in patients with total knee arthroplasty: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Kwak SG; Kwon JB; Bae JW; Bae DJ; Kim DK; Choi WK
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: CONCLUSION: The administration of IV iron supplements during or after TKA surgery increases hemoglobin recovery between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery and reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusion during hospitalization.
all_evidence.outcome: Second, to examine whether the administration of IV iron supplements during or immediately after TKA in patients undergoing primary TKA can reduce the need for allogenic blood transfusion during hospitalization. | The population, intervention, comparison, and outcome of this study are as follows; Population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty; Intervention: Administration of IV iron supplements during or immediately after surgery; Comparison: Non-administration of IV iron supplements; Outcome: Degree of hemoglobin recovery (between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery) and the need for blood transfusion during hospitalization. | There was a statistically significant difference for post-operative transfusion rate between 2 groups.
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: The administration of IV iron supplements during or after TKA surgery increases hemoglobin recovery between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery and reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusion during hospitalization.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 결론: 슬관절 전치환술 중 또는 이후의 정맥 철분 보충제 투여는 수술 4주에서 8주 사이의 헤모글로빈 회복을 증가시키고 입원 중 동종 수혈 필요성을 감소시킨다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: The objectives of the researchers are as follows: First, to investigate whether intraoperative or postoperative administration of Intravenous (IV) iron supplements in patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) can contribute to the hemoglobin recovery during the postoperative period (between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery). | The population, intervention, comparison, and outcome of this study are as follows; Population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty; Intervention: Administration of IV iron supplements during or immediately after surgery; Comparison: Non-administration of IV iron supplements; Outcome: Degree of hemoglobin recovery (between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery) and the need for blood transfusion during hospitalization. | CONCLUSION: The administration of IV iron supplements during or after TKA surgery increases hemoglobin recovery between 4 and 8 weeks after surgery and reduces the need for allogeneic blood transfusion during hospitalization.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative intravenous versus oral iron supplementation for elective surgery: evidence based on 12 randomized trials.
all_evidence.authors: Yue L; Zhang J; Li C; Wang Z; Qi L; Zhao Y; Wang S; Shang M; Li C; Sun H
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: IVIS was associated with fewer digestive (RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) but more pain-related adverse events (RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.outcome: AIM: This study aims to clarify hematological parameters, transfusion requirements, and adverse events of preoperative intravenous (IVIS) versus oral iron supplementation (OIS) in elective surgery patients. | Our analysis focused on post-treatment hemoglobin levels, changes in hemoglobin from baseline, ferritin levels, hemoglobin attainment rates, transfusion requirements, and adverse events. | No significant differences were noted in transfusion rates or volumes.
all_evidence.key_finding: IVIS was associated with fewer digestive (RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) but more pain-related adverse events (RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 정맥 철분 보충은 소화기계 이상반응은 더 적었으나(RR = 0.10, 95% CI [0.05 to 0.22]; I2 = 0%) 통증 관련 이상반응은 더 많았다(RR = 7.79, 95% CI [1.78 to 34.07]; I2 = 0%).
all_evidence.population: AIM: This study aims to clarify hematological parameters, transfusion requirements, and adverse events of preoperative intravenous (IVIS) versus oral iron supplementation (OIS) in elective surgery patients. | INTERPRETATION: IVIS offers a superior improvement in hematological parameters for elective surgery patients but not reducing transfusion needs compared to OIS.

all_evidence.title: Preoperative iron supplementation in non-anemic patients undergoing major surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Toledo FV; De Carli D; Meletti JFA; Togo HYA; Gomes IP; Sakashita RM; Montes LF; Tiburcio RS; Miranda CA
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Preoperative iron supplementation was associated with a significantly lower risk of receiving a blood transfusion (OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Blood transfusions are associated with increased morbidity and mortality, and maintaining global blood supplies can be a challenge. | This systematic review investigates the impact of preoperative iron supplementation on the risk of blood transfusion among non-anemic patients undergoing major surgeries. | Outcomes assessed included the number of individuals who received blood transfusions, and mean hemoglobin levels at the first day and by the first postoperative week.
all_evidence.key_finding: Preoperative iron supplementation was associated with a significantly lower risk of receiving a blood transfusion (OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 수술 전 철분 보충은 수혈을 받을 위험이 유의하게 더 낮은 것과 관련이 있었다(OR = 0.54; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.75; p < 0.001).
all_evidence.population: This systematic review investigates the impact of preoperative iron supplementation on the risk of blood transfusion among non-anemic patients undergoing major surgeries. | Outcomes assessed included the number of individuals who received blood transfusions, and mean hemoglobin levels at the first day and by the first postoperative week. | Of these, 54% received preoperative iron supplementation.

evidence.population: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intravenous iron is a key component of anemia management for chronic kidney disease (CKD). | Anemic patients with CKD stage 5D on hemodialysis and on a stable erythropoiesis-stimulating agent regimen received either two injections of 510 mg of ferumoxytol within 7 d (n = 114) or 200 mg elemental oral iron daily for 21 d (n = 116). | CONCLUSIONS: In patients on hemodialysis, rapid intravenous injection of 510 mg of ferumoxytol led to significantly greater hemoglobin increases compared with oral iron, with comparable tolerability.

evidence.population: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Intravenous iron is a key component of anemia management for chronic kidney disease (CKD). | Anemic patients with CKD stage 5D on hemodialysis and on a stable erythropoiesis-stimulating agent regimen received either two injections of 510 mg of ferumoxytol within 7 d (n = 114) or 200 mg elemental oral iron daily for 21 d (n = 116). | CONCLUSIONS: In patients on hemodialysis, rapid intravenous injection of 510 mg of ferumoxytol led to significantly greater hemoglobin increases compared with oral iron, with comparable tolerability.

all_evidence.title: Homocysteine as a risk factor for cardiovascular disease in patients treated by dialysis: a meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Heinz J; Kropf S; Luley C; Dierkes J
all_evidence.venue: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The pooled overall risk estimate for prospective observational studies suggests no association between homocysteine level (5-micromol/L increase) and total mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.02; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.12; P = 0.7), but there was an association with cardiovascular events (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.14; P = 0.001).
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: In the general population, increased homocysteine concentrations are a risk factor for cardiovascular disease and mortality. | SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: Studies investigating the association between total homocysteine level and cardiovascular disease or total mortality or the influence of vitamin supplementation on cardiovascular or mortality risk. | OUTCOMES: In retrospective studies, cases are patients with cardiovascular diseases.
all_evidence.key_finding: The pooled overall risk estimate for prospective observational studies suggests no association between homocysteine level (5-micromol/L increase) and total mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.02; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.12; P = 0.7), but there was an association with cardiovascular events (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.14; P = 0.001).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 전향적 관찰연구를 통합한 전체 위험 추정치는 호모시스테인 수치(5-micromol/L 증가)와 전체 사망률 사이에 관련이 없음을 시사했으나(위험비[HR], 1.02; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.12; P = 0.7), 심혈관 사건과는 관련이 있었다(HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.03 to 1.14; P = 0.001).
all_evidence.population: However, it is not known whether this also applies to patients with end-stage renal disease. | STUDY DESIGN: Meta-analysis of retrospective (11 studies including 1,506 individuals), prospective observational studies (12 studies including 1,975 individuals), and intervention trials (5 studies including 1,642 dialysis patients). | SETTING & POPULATION: Studies of patients with end-stage renal disease treated by means of hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

evidence.title: Prenatal multivitamin supplementation and rates of congenital anomalies: a meta-analysis.
evidence.authors: Ingrid Goh Y; Bollano E; Einarson TR; Koren G
evidence.venue: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the protective effect of folic acid-fortified multivitamin supplements on other congenital anomalies. | Using a random effects model, rates of congenital anomalies in babies born to women who were taking multivitamin supplements were compared with rates in the offspring of controls who were not. | For cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.93), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.42 (95% CI 0.06-2.84); for oral cleft with or without cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.58 (95% CI 0.28-1.19); for urinary tract anomalies, case control studies showed OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.30-0.76), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.68 (95% CI 0.35-1.31); and for congenital hydrocephalus case control studies showed OR 0.37 (95% CI 0.24-0.56), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 1.54 (95% CI 0.53-4.50).
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.

evidence.population: Several studies have also proposed the effectiveness of these supplements in preventing other birth defects; however, such effects have never been systematically examined. | METHODS: We searched Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, Toxline, Healthstar, and Cochrane databases for studies describing the outcome of pregnancies in women using multivitamin supplements that were published in all languages from January 1966 to July 2005. | CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.

all_evidence.title: The Impact of Minerals on Female Fertility: A Systematic Review.
all_evidence.authors: Kapper C; Stelzl P; Oppelt P; Ganhör C; Gyunesh AA; Arbeithuber B; Rezk-Füreder M
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted role of minerals in female fertility, focusing on key areas such as oocyte quality, ovulation, embryo development, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, environmental exposure, and in-vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. | Relevant literature was sourced from multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, using keywords related to minerals and female fertility. | The studies addressed various reproductive outcomes influenced by minerals: embryo development, oocyte quality, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, IVF outcomes, environmental exposure, and minerals as biomarkers.
all_evidence.key_finding: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.

all_evidence.population: METHODS: A systematic review was conducted, focusing on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, case-control studies, nested case-control, and observational studies examining mineral supplementation and nutrition in women planning pregnancy or utilizing assisted reproduction technologies (ARTs).

all_evidence.title: Magnesium supplementation in pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Makrides M; Crosby DD; Bain E; Crowther CA
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_13: One trial contributed over 70% of the participants to the analysis for this outcome; the trial authors suggested that the large number of severe congenital anomalies in the supplemented group (unlikely attributable to magnesium) and the deaths of two sets of twins (with birthweights < 750 g) in the supplemented group likely accounted for the increased risk of death observed, and thus this result should be interpreted with caution.
all_evidence.outcome: The primary outcomes were perinatal mortality (including stillbirth and neonatal death prior to hospital discharge), small-for-gestational age, maternal mortality and pre-eclampsia. | In the 10 included trials, the compositions of the magnesium supplements, gestational ages at commencement, and doses administered varied, including: magnesium oxide, 1000 mg daily from ≤ four months post-conception (one trial); magnesium citrate, 365 mg daily from ≤ 18 weeks until hospitalisation after 38 weeks (one trial), and 340 mg daily from nine to 27 weeks' gestation (one trial); magnesium gluconate, 2 to 3 g from 28 weeks' gestation until birth (one trial), and 4 g daily from 23 weeks' gestation (one trial); magnesium aspartate, 15 mmol daily (three trials, commencing from either six to 21 weeks' gestation until birth, ≤ 16 weeks' gestation until birth, or < 12 weeks until birth), or 365 mg daily from 13 to 24 weeks until birth (one trial); and magnesium stearate, 128 mg elemental magnesium from 10 to 35 weeks until birth (one trial).In the analysis of all trials, oral magnesium supplementation compared to no magnesium was associated with no significant difference in perinatal mortality (stillbirth and neonatal death prior to discharge) (risk ratio (RR) 1.10; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.72 to 1.67; five trials, 5903 infants), small-for-gestational age (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.54 to 1.07; three trials, 1291 infants), or pre-eclampsia (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.58 to 1.32; three trials, 1042 women). | None of the included trials reported on maternal mortality.Considering secondary outcomes, while no increased risk of stillbirth was observed, a possible increased risk of neonatal death prior to hospital discharge was shown for infants born to mothers who had received magnesium (RR 2.21; 95% CI 1.02 to 4.75; four trials, 5373 infants).
all_evidence.key_finding: One trial contributed over 70% of the participants to the analysis for this outcome; the trial authors suggested that the large number of severe congenital anomalies in the supplemented group (unlikely attributable to magnesium) and the deaths of two sets of twins (with birthweights < 750 g) in the supplemented group likely accounted for the increased risk of death observed, and thus this result should be interpreted with caution.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 이 결과변수 분석에서 참가자의 70% 이상을 한 개 시험이 제공했다. 해당 시험 저자들은 보충군에서 나타난 다수의 중증 선천기형(마그네슘에 기인할 가능성은 낮음)과 보충군에서 발생한 쌍둥이 2쌍(출생체중 < 750 g)의 사망이 관찰된 사망 위험 증가를 설명할 가능성이 높다고 제시했으므로, 이 결과는 신중하게 해석해야 한다.

all_evidence.title: Intermittent oral iron supplementation during pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Peña-Rosas JP; De-Regil LM; Gomez Malave H; Flores-Urrutia MC; Dowswell T
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_11: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.outcome: None of the studies reported congenital anomalies.For maternal outcomes, there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for anaemia at term (average RR 1.22; 95% CI 0.84 to 1.80; participants = 676; studies = four; I² = 10%; very low quality). | There were no clear differences between groups for mean birthweight, preterm birth, maternal anaemia or maternal side effects.
all_evidence.key_finding: The methodological quality of included studies was mixed and most had high levels of attrition.The overall assessment of the quality of the evidence for primary infant outcomes was low and for maternal outcomes very low.Of the 21 trials contributing data, three studies provided intermittent iron alone, 14 intermittent iron + folic acid and four intermittent iron plus multiple vitamins and minerals in comparison with the same composition of supplements provided in a daily regimen.Overall, for women receiving any intermittent iron regimen (with or without other vitamins and minerals) compared with a daily regimen there was no clear evidence of differences between groups for any infant primary outcomes: low birthweight (average risk ratio (RR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55 to 1.22; participants = 1898; studies = eight; low quality evidence), infant birthweight (mean difference (MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; participants = 1939; studies = nine; low quality evidence), premature birth (average RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; participants = 1177; studies = five; low quality evidence), or neonatal death (average RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; participants = 795; studies = one; very low quality).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 포함된 연구의 방법론적 질은 혼재돼 있었고 대부분 탈락률이 높았다. 일차 영아 결과변수에 대한 근거의 질은 전반적으로 낮았고 모체 결과변수는 매우 낮았다. 자료를 제공한 21개 시험 중 3개는 간헐적 철분 단독, 14개는 간헐적 철분 + 엽산, 4개는 간헐적 철분과 다중 비타민·무기질을 같은 조성의 매일 요법과 비교했다. 전반적으로 간헐적 철분 요법(다른 비타민·무기질 병용 여부 무관)을 받은 여성은 매일 요법과 비교해 어떤 일차 영아 결과변수에서도 군 간 차이의 뚜렷한 근거가 없었다: 저체중출생(평균 위험비(RR) 0.82; 95% 신뢰구간(CI) 0.55 to 1.22; 참가자 = 1898; 연구 = 8개; 낮은 질 근거), 영아 출생체중(평균차(MD) 5.13 g; 95% CI -29.46 to 39.72; 참가자 = 1939; 연구 = 9개; 낮은 질 근거), 조산(평균 RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.76 to 1.39; 참가자 = 1177; 연구 = 5개; 낮은 질 근거), 신생아 사망(평균 RR 0.49; 95% CI 0.04 to 5.42; 참가자 = 795; 연구 = 1개; 매우 낮은 질).

all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Anaemia is a frequent condition during pregnancy, particularly among women in low- and middle-income countries. | Traditionally, gestational anaemia has been prevented with daily iron supplements throughout pregnancy, but adherence to this regimen due to side effects, interrupted supply of the supplements, and concerns about safety among women with an adequate iron intake, have limited the use of this intervention. | OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of intermittent supplementation with iron alone or in combination with folic acid or other vitamins and minerals to pregnant women on neonatal and pregnancy outcomes.

all_evidence.title: Adherence to iron-folic acid supplementation among pregnant women in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Sendeku FW; Azeze GG; Fenta SL
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Having secondary and above educational status of the women (AOR:2.68,95%CI:1.25, 5.74), having an early registration of antenatal care follow-up (≤16 weeks) (AOR:2.54,95%CI:1.99, 3.24), having anemia complication during current pregnancy (AOR:3.01,95%CI:1.88, 4.81), having good knowledge of iron-folic acid supplementation (AOR: 2.96, 95%CI:1.76, 4.99), having four times or more antenatal care follow up (AOR:3.66, 95%CI:2.81, 4.77), getting health education about benefit of iron and folic acid (AOR:2.62,95%CI:1.46,4.72), and having good knowledge about anemia (AOR:2.99,95%CI:2.32, 3.85) were associated risk factors for adherence to iron-folic acid supplementation.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND: Despite the supplementation of iron-folic acid is the recommended strategy during the antenatal period; iron deficiency anemia is the commonest hematologic complication during pregnancy. | Having secondary and above educational status of the women (AOR:2.68,95%CI:1.25, 5.74), having an early registration of antenatal care follow-up (≤16 weeks) (AOR:2.54,95%CI:1.99, 3.24), having anemia complication during current pregnancy (AOR:3.01,95%CI:1.88, 4.81), having good knowledge of iron-folic acid supplementation (AOR: 2.96, 95%CI:1.76, 4.99), having four times or more antenatal care follow up (AOR:3.66, 95%CI:2.81, 4.77), getting health education about benefit of iron and folic acid (AOR:2.62,95%CI:1.46,4.72), and having good knowledge about anemia (AOR:2.99,95%CI:2.32, 3.85) were associated risk factors for adherence to iron-folic acid supplementation. | This finding is important to design strategic policies and to prevent anemia and congenital anomaly resulted from inadequate intake of iron and folic acid.
all_evidence.key_finding: Having secondary and above educational status of the women (AOR:2.68,95%CI:1.25, 5.74), having an early registration of antenatal care follow-up (≤16 weeks) (AOR:2.54,95%CI:1.99, 3.24), having anemia complication during current pregnancy (AOR:3.01,95%CI:1.88, 4.81), having good knowledge of iron-folic acid supplementation (AOR: 2.96, 95%CI:1.76, 4.99), having four times or more antenatal care follow up (AOR:3.66, 95%CI:2.81, 4.77), getting health education about benefit of iron and folic acid (AOR:2.62,95%CI:1.46,4.72), and having good knowledge about anemia (AOR:2.99,95%CI:2.32, 3.85) were associated risk factors for adherence to iron-folic acid supplementation.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 여성의 중등 이상 학력(AOR:2.68,95%CI:1.25, 5.74), 산전관리 조기 등록(≤16주)(AOR:2.54,95%CI:1.99, 3.24), 현재 임신 중 빈혈 합병증(AOR:3.01,95%CI:1.88, 4.81), 철분-엽산 보충에 대한 좋은 지식(AOR: 2.96, 95%CI:1.76, 4.99), 산전관리 4회 이상 방문(AOR:3.66, 95%CI:2.81, 4.77), 철분과 엽산의 이점에 대한 보건교육 수령(AOR:2.62,95%CI:1.46,4.72), 빈혈에 대한 좋은 지식(AOR:2.99,95%CI:2.32, 3.85)이 철분-엽산 보충 순응도와 관련된 위험 요인이었다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Despite the supplementation of iron-folic acid is the recommended strategy during the antenatal period; iron deficiency anemia is the commonest hematologic complication during pregnancy. | Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the level of adherence to iron-folic acid supplementation and its associated factors among pregnant women in Ethiopia. | RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis with a total of 5808 pregnant women.

all_evidence.title: The effects of oral ferrous bisglycinate supplementation on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations in adults and children: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
all_evidence.authors: Fischer JAJ; Cherian AM; Bone JN; Karakochuk CD
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.outcome: Iron salts are commonly provided as oral supplements to prevent and treat iron deficiency, despite poor bioavailability and frequently reported adverse side effects. | Ferrous bisglycinate is a novel amino acid iron chelate that is thought to be more bioavailable and associated with fewer gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events as compared with iron salts. | OBJECTIVE: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted to evaluate the effects of ferrous bisglycinate supplementation compared with other iron supplements on hemoglobin and ferritin concentrations and GI adverse events.
all_evidence.key_finding: DATA ANALYSIS: Compared with other iron supplements, supplementation with ferrous bisglycinate for 4-20 weeks resulted in higher hemoglobin concentrations in pregnant women (SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01) and fewer reported GI adverse events (IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01).
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 자료 분석: 다른 철분 보충제와 비교해 4-20주간의 페러스 비스글리시네이트 보충은 임신부에서 더 높은 헤모글로빈 농도(SMD, 0.54 g/dL; 95% 신뢰구간[CI], 0.15-0.94; P < 0.01)와 더 적은 위장관 이상반응 보고(IRR, 0.36; 95%CI, 0.17-0.76; P < 0.01)로 이어졌다.
all_evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
all_evidence.population: CONTEXT: Iron deficiency and anemia have serious consequences, especially for children and pregnant women. | DATA EXTRACTION: Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted among trials of pregnant women (n = 9) and children (n = 4); pooled estimates were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs). | The remaining trials in other populations (n = 4; men and nonpregnant women) were qualitatively evaluated.

all_evidence.title: The Efficacy and Safety of Myo-inositol Supplementation for the Prevention of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Overweight and Obese Pregnant Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
all_evidence.authors: Factor PA; Corpuz H
all_evidence.venue: Journal of the ASEAN Federation of Endocrine Societies
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_14: While studies show that 4 g myo-inositol per day may decrease the incidence of GDM, pregnancy-induced hypertension and pre-term birth with no associated risk of serious adverse events, the certainty of evidence is low to very low.
all_evidence.outcome: Secondary outcomes included cesarean section rate, the incidence of pregnancy-induced hypertension, macrosomia and preterm delivery. | No adverse effects were noted. | For the secondary outcomes, standard dose myo-inositol appears to reduce the incidence of pregnancy-induced hypertension and preterm delivery, but the certainty of evidence is low to very low.
all_evidence.key_finding: While studies show that 4 g myo-inositol per day may decrease the incidence of GDM, pregnancy-induced hypertension and pre-term birth with no associated risk of serious adverse events, the certainty of evidence is low to very low.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 하루 미오이노시톨 4 g이 임신성 당뇨병, 임신성 고혈압, 조산 발생을 감소시키면서 중대한 이상반응 위험은 동반하지 않을 수 있다는 연구들이 있으나, 근거의 확실성은 낮음에서 매우 낮음 수준이다.
all_evidence.population: BACKGROUND: Myo-inositol has emerged as one of the preventive therapies for the development of gestational diabetes mellitus in at-risk populations. | This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to determine the efficacy and safety of myo-inositol in decreasing the incidence of gestational diabetes in overweight and obese pregnant women. | Inclusion criteria were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that enrolled overweight and obese pregnant women and used myo-inositol supplementation.

all_evidence.title: The prevention of congenital anomalies with periconceptional folic acid supplementation.
all_evidence.authors: McDonald SD; Ferguson S; Tam L; Lougheed J; Walker MC
all_evidence.venue: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_5: Since 1998, mandatory fortification of certain foods with folate has been associated with at least a 54% reduction in the incidence of open neural tube defects, yet rates of periconceptional folic acid use remain suboptimal, especially in minority women.
all_evidence.outcome: Furthermore, a reduction in the incidence of congenital cardiac and urologic anomalies has been demonstrated in some studies following periconceptional folic acid supplementation. | There is growing evidence of a possible role of folic acid supplementation in the prevention of other congenital anomalies, including cardiac defects.
all_evidence.key_finding: Since 1998, mandatory fortification of certain foods with folate has been associated with at least a 54% reduction in the incidence of open neural tube defects, yet rates of periconceptional folic acid use remain suboptimal, especially in minority women.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 1998년 이후 특정 식품에 대한 엽산 의무 강화는 개방성 신경관결손 발생을 최소 54% 감소시킨 것과 관련이 있었으나, 임신 전후 엽산 사용률은 특히 소수인종 여성에서 여전히 미흡하다.
all_evidence.population: Since 1992, a number of national and international professional societies have released guidelines recommending folic acid supplementation of at least 0.4 mg/day for all women of childbearing age or women planning pregnancies, and 4 mg/day for women with a previous infant with a neural tube defect.

all_evidence.title: Effectiveness and safety of vitamin D in relation to bone health.
all_evidence.authors: Cranney A; Horsley T; O'Donnell S; Weiler H; Puil L; Ooi D; Atkinson S; Ward L; Moher D; Hanley D; Fang M; Yazdi F; Garritty C; Sampson M; Barrowman N; Tsertsvadze A; Mamaladze V
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_1: OBJECTIVES: To review and synthesize the literature in the following areas: the association of specific circulating 25(OH)D concentrations with bone health outcomes in children, women of reproductive age, postmenopausal women and elderly men; the effect of dietary intakes (foods fortified with vitamin D and/or vitamin D supplementation) and sun exposure on serum 25(OH)D; the effect of vitamin D on bone mineral density (BMD) and fracture or fall risk; and the identification of potential harms of vitamin D above current reference intakes.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: To review and synthesize the literature in the following areas: the association of specific circulating 25(OH)D concentrations with bone health outcomes in children, women of reproductive age, postmenopausal women and elderly men; the effect of dietary intakes (foods fortified with vitamin D and/or vitamin D supplementation) and sun exposure on serum 25(OH)D; the effect of vitamin D on bone mineral density (BMD) and fracture or fall risk; and the identification of potential harms of vitamin D above current reference intakes. | REVIEW METHODS: Two independent reviewers completed a multi-level process of screening the literature to identify eligible studies (title and abstract, followed by full text review, and categorization of study design per key question). | Vitamin D intake above current dietary reference intakes was not reported to be associated with an increased risk of adverse events.
all_evidence.key_finding: OBJECTIVES: To review and synthesize the literature in the following areas: the association of specific circulating 25(OH)D concentrations with bone health outcomes in children, women of reproductive age, postmenopausal women and elderly men; the effect of dietary intakes (foods fortified with vitamin D and/or vitamin D supplementation) and sun exposure on serum 25(OH)D; the effect of vitamin D on bone mineral density (BMD) and fracture or fall risk; and the identification of potential harms of vitamin D above current reference intakes.

all_evidence.population: There were very few studies in pregnant and lactating women, and insufficient evidence for an association between serum 25(OH)D and changes in BMD during lactation, and fair evidence of an inverse correlation with PTH.

all_evidence.title: Bovine Colostrum for Preterm Infants in the First Days of Life: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial.

all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that it is feasible to use BC as a supplement to MM during the first weeks of life to increase enteral protein intake in preterm infants.
all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVES: Mother's own milk (MM) is the best nutrition for newborn preterm infants, but is often limited in supply just after birth. | Pasteurized human donor milk (DM), and especially preterm infant formula (IF) are less optimal diets than MM. | We hypothesized that it is feasible to use bovine colostrum (BC), the first milk from cows, as a supplement to MM, during the first weeks after preterm birth.
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that it is feasible to use BC as a supplement to MM during the first weeks of life to increase enteral protein intake in preterm infants.

evidence.title: Prenatal multivitamin supplementation and rates of congenital anomalies: a meta-analysis.
evidence.authors: Ingrid Goh Y; Bollano E; Einarson TR; Koren G
evidence.venue: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_12: CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the protective effect of folic acid-fortified multivitamin supplements on other congenital anomalies. | Using a random effects model, rates of congenital anomalies in babies born to women who were taking multivitamin supplements were compared with rates in the offspring of controls who were not. | For cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.93), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.42 (95% CI 0.06-2.84); for oral cleft with or without cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.58 (95% CI 0.28-1.19); for urinary tract anomalies, case control studies showed OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.30-0.76), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.68 (95% CI 0.35-1.31); and for congenital hydrocephalus case control studies showed OR 0.37 (95% CI 0.24-0.56), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 1.54 (95% CI 0.53-4.50).
evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 결론: 엽산 함유 산전 종합비타민의 모체 섭취는 신경관결손뿐 아니라 여러 선천기형의 위험 감소와 관련이 있다.
evidence.publication_types: Journal Article|Meta-Analysis|Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't|Systematic Review
evidence.population: Several studies have also proposed the effectiveness of these supplements in preventing other birth defects; however, such effects have never been systematically examined. | METHODS: We searched Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, Toxline, Healthstar, and Cochrane databases for studies describing the outcome of pregnancies in women using multivitamin supplements that were published in all languages from January 1966 to July 2005. | CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.

evidence.title: Herbal Medicinal Product Use During Pregnancy and the Postnatal Period: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Muñoz Balbontín Y; Stewart D; Shetty A; Fitton CA; McLay JS
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_9: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.
evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: To report the incidence and nature of herbal medicinal products' adverse events and herb-drug interactions used by some pregnant and postnatal women. | DATA SOURCES: The Allied and Complementary Medicine Database, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, EMBASE, the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until August 2018. | METHODS OF STUDY SELECTION: Any studies reporting adverse events, herb-drug interactions or absence thereof associated with herbal medicinal products used during pregnancy or the postnatal period were included.
evidence.key_finding: Adverse drug reactions, congenital malformations, fetal growth retardation or herb-drug interactions were the primary study objective reported by 19 of the 74 included studies, 16 cohort studies, one cross-sectional survey, and two randomized controlled trials.

evidence.title: The Impact of Minerals on Female Fertility: A Systematic Review.
evidence.authors: Kapper C; Stelzl P; Oppelt P; Ganhör C; Gyunesh AA; Arbeithuber B; Rezk-Füreder M
evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.
evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted role of minerals in female fertility, focusing on key areas such as oocyte quality, ovulation, embryo development, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, environmental exposure, and in-vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. | Relevant literature was sourced from multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, using keywords related to minerals and female fertility. | The studies addressed various reproductive outcomes influenced by minerals: embryo development, oocyte quality, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, IVF outcomes, environmental exposure, and minerals as biomarkers.
evidence.key_finding: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.
evidence.key_finding_ko: 분석 결과 셀레늄, 아연, 구리 같은 무기질은 생식 건강 유지에 필수적인 반면 카드뮴, 납 같은 독성 금속에 대한 노출은 해로운 것으로 나타났다.
evidence.population: METHODS: A systematic review was conducted, focusing on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, case-control studies, nested case-control, and observational studies examining mineral supplementation and nutrition in women planning pregnancy or utilizing assisted reproduction technologies (ARTs).

all_evidence.outcome: OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the protective effect of folic acid-fortified multivitamin supplements on other congenital anomalies. | Using a random effects model, rates of congenital anomalies in babies born to women who were taking multivitamin supplements were compared with rates in the offspring of controls who were not. | For cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.93), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.42 (95% CI 0.06-2.84); for oral cleft with or without cleft palate, case control studies showed OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.58 (95% CI 0.28-1.19); for urinary tract anomalies, case control studies showed OR 0.48 (95% CI 0.30-0.76), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 0.68 (95% CI 0.35-1.31); and for congenital hydrocephalus case control studies showed OR 0.37 (95% CI 0.24-0.56), and cohort and randomized controlled studies showed OR 1.54 (95% CI 0.53-4.50).
all_evidence.key_finding: CONCLUSION: Maternal consumption of folic acid-containing prenatal multivitamins is associated with decreased risk for several congenital anomalies, not only neural tube defects.

all_evidence.title: The Impact of Minerals on Female Fertility: A Systematic Review.
all_evidence.authors: Kapper C; Stelzl P; Oppelt P; Ganhör C; Gyunesh AA; Arbeithuber B; Rezk-Füreder M
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_10: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.
all_evidence.outcome: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the multifaceted role of minerals in female fertility, focusing on key areas such as oocyte quality, ovulation, embryo development, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, environmental exposure, and in-vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. | Relevant literature was sourced from multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, using keywords related to minerals and female fertility. | The studies addressed various reproductive outcomes influenced by minerals: embryo development, oocyte quality, oxidative stress, miscarriage, hormonal regulation, IVF outcomes, environmental exposure, and minerals as biomarkers.
all_evidence.key_finding: The analysis revealed that minerals like selenium, zinc, and copper are essential for maintaining reproductive health, while exposure to toxic metals such as cadmium and lead is detrimental.
all_evidence.key_finding_ko: 분석 결과 셀레늄, 아연, 구리 같은 무기질은 생식 건강 유지에 필수적인 반면 카드뮴, 납 같은 독성 금속에 대한 노출은 해로운 것으로 나타났다.
all_evidence.population: METHODS: A systematic review was conducted, focusing on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, case-control studies, nested case-control, and observational studies examining mineral supplementation and nutrition in women planning pregnancy or utilizing assisted reproduction technologies (ARTs).

all_evidence.title: Magnesium supplementation in pregnancy.
all_evidence.authors: Makrides M; Crosby DD; Bain E; Crowther CA
all_evidence.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
all_evidence.locator: ABSTRACT_SENTENCE_13: One trial contributed over 70% of the participants to the analysis for this outcome; the trial authors suggested that the large number of severe congenital anomalies in the supplemented group (unlikely attributable to magnesium) and the deaths of two sets of twins (with birthweights < 750 g) in the supplemented group likely accounted for the increased risk of death observed, and thus this result should be interpreted with caution.
all_evidence.outcome: The primary outcomes were perinatal mortality (including stillbirth and neonatal death prior to hospital discharge), small-for-gestational age, maternal mortality and pre-eclampsia. | In the 10 included trials, the compositions of the magnesium supplements, gestational ages at commencement, and doses administered varied, including: magnesium oxide, 1000 mg daily from ≤ four months post-conception (one trial); magnesium citrate, 365 mg daily from ≤ 18 weeks until hospitalisation after 38 weeks (one trial), and 340 mg daily from nine to 27 weeks' gestation (one trial); magnesium gluconate, 2 to 3 g from 28 weeks' gestation until birth (one trial), and 4 g daily from 23 weeks' gestation (one trial); magnesium aspartate, 15 mmol daily (three trials, commencing from either six to 21 weeks' gestation until birth, ≤ 16 weeks' gestation until birth, or < 12 weeks until birth), or 365 mg daily from 13 to 24 weeks until birth (one trial); and magnesium stearate, 128 mg elemental magnesium from 10 to 35 weeks until birth (one trial).In the analysis of all trials, oral magnesium supplementation compared to no magnesium was associated with no significant difference in perinatal mortality (stillbirth and neonatal death prior to discharge) (risk ratio (RR) 1.10; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.72 to 1.67; five trials, 5903 infants), small-for-gestational age (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.54 to 1.07; three trials, 1291 infants), or pre-eclampsia (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.58 to 1.32; three trials, 1042 women). | None of the included trials reported on maternal mortality.Considering secondary outcomes, while no increased risk of stillbirth was observed, a possible increased risk of neonatal death prior to hospital discharge was shown for infants born to mothers who had received magnesium (RR 2.21; 95% CI 1.02 to 4.75; four trials, 5373 infants).
all_evidence.key_finding: One trial contributed over 70% of the participants to the analysis for this outcome; the trial authors suggested that the large number of severe congenital anomalies in the supplemented group (unlikely attributable to magnesium) and the deaths of two sets of twins (with birthweights < 750 g) in the supplemented group likely accounted for the increased risk of death observed, and thus this result should be interpreted with caution.
